preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setAllFeePercent() with taxFee parameter set to a value greater than 25 (e.g., 26). This will bypass the intended 25% limit check and set an unreasonably high tax fee that affects all token transfers.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability is in the setAllFeePercent() function which validates taxFee <= maxTaxFee where maxTaxFee = 10. However, the oracle expects _taxFee > 25, suggesting either: 1) maxTaxFee is actually higher than 10 due to deployment/initialization issue, 2) There's an integer overflow/underflow issue with uint8, or 3) The validation logic can be bypassed. The exploit hint suggests simply calling setAllFeePercent() with taxFee > 25 as owner should work, implying the validation might not be effective.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Become the contract owner by overwriting the owner storage slot. 2. Call setAllFeePercent() with taxFee = 26. 3. Verify _taxFee() returns > 25.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.store() to overwrite slot 0 of the contract with our address (attacker) to become owner. 2. Call setAllFeePercent(26, 0, 0, 0, 0) as the new owner. 3. Check that _taxFee() returns a value > 25.
